chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who divorces his wife during a period of purity, without sexual intercourse, then revives her during that same day, then divorces her again, so that three divorces are completed from him during one period of purity. He said: 'He acted contrary to the Sunnah.' I said: 'So it is not befitting for him, when he revives her, to divorce her except during a period of purity?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Until he has sexual intercourse with her?' He said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.السُّنَّة: The Prophetic tradition or established practice
key_terms.تَبِين: To become clear/definitive (referring to the completion of three divorces)
key_terms.مُرَاجَعَة: Revival (restoring the wife to the marital state after a revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct procedure for a man to effect three divorces if he divorces his wife without sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural validity of triple divorce (talaq al-thalath) by establishing that sexual intercourse (jima') is a prerequisite for resetting the 'period of purity' (tuhr) cycle. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on strict adherence to the Sunnah, where divorcing without prior consummation in that specific cycle is considered a deviation, thereby ensuring the three divorces are distinct and valid.
